messages.subject: 2-1-1 SEM model with continuous outcomes and binary predictor
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm doing a SEM model in a longitudinal study (n = 271) with a binary IV at level 2 and various continuous predictors at level 1 (cluster in 22 classrooms).

However, I repeatedly got this error: 

Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  : 
  lavaan ERROR
    Some between-level (only) variables have non-zero variance at the
    within-level. Please double-check your data.

De plus : Warning messages:
1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Level-1 variable “T2EMOPOSIT” has no variance within some
    clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: 303
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Level-2 variable “COND” has non-zero variance at the within level.
    The cluster ids with non-zero within variance are: 707A 304

Thank you very much for your help!

Jordane

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: 2-1-1 SEM model with continuous outcomes and binary predictor
parts:
Some between-level (only) variables have non-zero variance at the
    within-level. Please double-check your data.

Are you including Level-2 variables in your Level-1 model?  Level-2 variables do not vary at Level-1, so they can not be part of the Level-1 covariance-structure model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.subject: Re: 2-1-1 SEM model with continuous outcomes and binary predictor
parts:
2: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Level-2 variable “COND” has non-zero variance at the within level.
    The cluster ids with non-zero within variance are: 707A 304

This message from your original post suggests it was included in your Level-1 model.  Do you still get this warning with the syntax you posted?  Because it would indeed be strange if lavaan were complaining about this being a within-level variable when it does not appear in your within-level model.

1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Level-1 variable “T2EMOPOSIT” has no variance within some
    clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: 303

This message is pretty informative.  It is also only a warning (in case there might be a problem), not an error.  If your error message went away after excluding COND from the within-level model, then you should still be able to view your results.  Using lavaan's example data, you can see there is no actual problem (though a warning) when you set all values of x1 within a single cluster to the same value:

data(Demo.twolevel)
Demo.twolevel$x1[Demo.twolevel$cluster == 1L] <- 0
model <- '
    level: 1
        fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3
        fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3
    level: 2
        fb =~ y1 + y2 + y3
        fb ~ w1 + w2
'
fit <- sem(model, data = Demo.twolevel, cluster = "cluster")
